items.title: Project Zenith Windows 11 developer environment launches on AMD Ryzen AI Halo
items.content_text: Project Zenith, Microsoft’s preconfigured Windows 11 developer experience, is now available preinstalled on AMD Ryzen AI Halo powered by the Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495. It includes developer tools such as VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Python and WSL, and is positioned as a ready-to-use platform for local AI development.

items.title: SoftwareOne achieves Select tier in Anthropic’s Claude Partner Network
items.content_text: SoftwareOne announced that it achieved Select partner tier in Anthropic’s Claude Partner Network Services Track. The announcement cites more than 100 certified experts and says SoftwareOne helps customers integrate, govern, and scale Claude deployments across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

items.title: OpenAI Java SDK v4.102.0 adds agent scheduling APIs and GPT-6 Rosalind support
items.content_text: OpenAI’s Java SDK v4.102.0 adds agent scheduling API support and recognizes GPT-6 Rosalind in beta Responses. This is a developer tooling update, not by itself confirmation that the model is generally available.

items.title: OpenAI Go SDK v3.98.0 adds GPT-6 Rosalind support and agent capabilities
items.content_text: OpenAI’s Go SDK v3.98.0 adds GPT-6 Rosalind to the beta Responses model constants and expands support for agent sessions, asynchronous function tools, SVG image editing, and Realtime audio controls. These are developer-platform updates; the SDK note alone does not establish that GPT-6 Rosalind is generally available.

items.title: Google Cloud makes DeepMind's Cloud Pathways runtime generally available
items.content_text: Cloud Pathways is now generally available on Google Kubernetes Engine for supported Cloud TPU environments. The distributed runtime, originally built by Google DeepMind to train and serve Gemini and other frontier models, lets customers orchestrate large accelerator fleets through a single controller.

items.title: Google announces TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max for agentic workloads
items.content_text: Google expanded its eighth-generation TPU lineup with TPU 8tx, designed for secure and confidential inference, and TPU 8i Max, designed for massive context windows and higher compute density. The systems add hardware options for agentic workloads and the infrastructure used to train and serve Gemini models.

items.title: NVIDIA announces investment in Point2 and planned investments in three Korean AI startups
items.content_text: NVIDIA announced an investment in Korean AI interconnect startup Point2 and said it plans additional investments in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD, and Upstage. The companies work across AI infrastructure, agent models, robotics, and enterprise AI, making the announcement a broad strategic investment in Korea’s AI ecosystem; amounts were not disclosed in the cited announcement.
tags: NVIDIA; Point2 Technology, Motif Technologies, RLWRLD, and Upstage

items.title: MIT-led team reports WorldParticle, a unified AI model for simulating diverse physical systems
items.content_text: Researchers from MIT, UBC, and collaborators reported WorldParticle, a single AI framework for simulating varied physical phenomena, from granular materials to proteins. They say it was tested on six phenomena and outperformed numerical simulation methods in accuracy in those demonstrations, suggesting a possible route to more general-purpose scientific simulation.
tags: Massachusetts Institute of Technology and University of British Columbia

items.title: MIT and NYU researchers introduce FLEX for robots to infer intent from natural-language commands
items.content_text: MIT and NYU researchers introduced FLEX, a robot motion-planning approach that uses natural-language instructions to infer broader preferences, such as avoiding nearby electronics after being told not to spill on a laptop. MIT reported demonstrations in simulated tasks; the approach could make robots easier to guide without users having to specify every rule individually.
tags: Massachusetts Institute of Technology and New York University

items.title: Google DeepMind science chief previews upcoming research releases
items.content_text: Google DeepMind VP of Science Pushmeet Kohli said the organization is seeing a marked acceleration in scientific discovery across its projects and expects upcoming releases to provide a glimpse of that progress. The post is a forward-looking research teaser and does not announce a specific result or product.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly commits $3.4 billion to gas-fired data-center generators
items.content_text: Anthropic reportedly agreed to pay about $3.4 billion for commitments to 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty gas-fired generators from OnePWR Solutions, including engineering and construction capabilities needed to install them. The unusually large procurement underscores how AI companies are securing power infrastructure directly as data-center demand grows; the deal was reportedly agreed in late September but became public in November 8 reporting.

items.title: U.S. AI safety center staff reportedly asked to report informally to White House
items.content_text: The Associated Press reported that officials at the Commerce Department’s AI safety center, CAISSI, were recently asked to report informally to a White House office, citing two former officials familiar with the discussions. The report raises questions about the center’s independence; it also says the center has no permanent leader and has stopped publishing research, so the reported change matters for federal AI safety oversight.

items.title: Microsoft paper reports Copilot harness results for complex task execution
items.content_text: A Microsoft Copilot Studio Blog paper reports that the Microsoft Copilot harness scored 65% against 36% for a leading competitor on a business-process benchmark. It also says telemetry-driven, one-tool-at-a-time tuning raised the Excel Online connector’s success rate from 85.6% to 96.3% without maker action, highlighting work on agent task execution and reliability.

items.title: GitHub анонсировал проекты в приложении Copilot для координации работы
items.content_text: GitHub рассказал о Projects в приложении Copilot: проект может объединять работу в одном или нескольких репозиториях, а также задачи, не привязанные к репозиторию. Copilot может запускать сессии, настраивать повторяющиеся автоматизации и создавать материалы, которые отображаются в проекте.

items.title: Anthropic employee clarifies customer notice about unauthorized access to account information
items.content_text: An Anthropic employee clarified that a customer notice concerned Cathedral’s unauthorized access through third-party software used by Anthropic. The post says the accessed information included business contact and basic account details, but not prompts, outputs, or payment details, and that Anthropic contained affected systems and worked with vendors to close vulnerabilities.

items.title: Microsoft Foundry blog outlines closed-loop evaluations for production agents
items.content_text: Microsoft published a guide to a closed-loop process for improving production agents, combining continuous evaluation and Application Insights signals with trace-based datasets, Agent Optimizer, regression tests, and CI/CD gates. The workflow also describes canary rollouts and promotion or rollback decisions, giving teams a way to evaluate agent quality and cost while controlling changes reaching users.

items.title: Microsoft releases five Windows 11 Insider builds with Search, privacy and Windows Hello updates
items.content_text: Microsoft announced five Windows 11 Insider preview builds across Beta and Experimental channels, including builds for 26H1 and Future Platforms. Notable changes include a redesigned Windows Search with inline actions, per-app desktop camera/microphone/location permissions, and Windows Hello sign-in and facial-recognition brightness improvements.

items.title: Microsoft introduces SharePoint MCP tools in Work IQ
items.content_text: Microsoft announced SharePoint MCP tools in preview for Work IQ, enabling custom apps and agents to discover and perform SharePoint tasks such as finding files, managing lists, and handling approvals. Calls use the signed-in user’s identity and permissions, and the tools use runtime discovery across a catalog of more than 60 operations.

items.title: Copilot code review adds API management and a more compact review overview
items.content_text: GitHub added REST and GraphQL API management for Copilot code-review settings, covering enterprise policy through individual repositories. The update also makes review summaries more compact and adds improvements for review credits, automatic-review bypasses, and repeated reviews.

items.title: Copilot impact dashboard adds Chat and VS Code agent usage
items.content_text: GitHub expanded the Copilot impact dashboard and enterprise/organization 28-day reports to track Copilot Chat and the VS Code Agents window, bringing the chart to nine experiences. It also renamed the “Passive users” cohort to “Chat-first users”; adoption-phase rules remain unchanged.

items.title: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — November 2
items.content_text: GitHub’s weekly Copilot release roundup described updates across its app, CLI, JetBrains, Xcode, and VS Code. Notable additions include Agent Merge controls in pull requests and VS Code local automations with cron expressions and workspace custom agents; the roundup also recaps Copilot’s IDE integrations and agent-session improvements.

items.title: @GitHub in Slack and Teams reaches general availability
items.content_text: GitHub made @GitHub in Slack and Teams generally available, enabling users to investigate bugs, create issues, implement changes, and open pull requests from conversations. Teams users can also review plans and code changes in Canvas, while onboarding and attribution were improved.

items.title: Claude Duet adds mobile control for Claude Code sessions
items.content_text: Claude Duet added support for Claude Code sessions, letting users check what is running, approve changes, and send updates from a phone for sessions on a computer or in the cloud. Duet’s builder also said the update supports steering Claude Code Projects.

items.title: Anthropic publishes Project EVE tests of Claude in MMORPGs
items.content_text: Anthropic reported Project EVE experiments in which Claude models traded in a simulated EVE Online market and teams of agents played EVE Frontier missions. The safety-relevant tests found that limited-access monitors detected only a minority of agents explicitly instructed to sabotage; Anthropic cautioned that this tested instructed behavior, not spontaneous inclination.

items.title: Anthropic describes “dreaming” as a way to organize agent memory
items.content_text: Anthropic described agent-memory components for Claude, including notes, salience judgments, and “dreaming”: offline reflection that can correct mistakes and reorganize or create memories across sessions. The post explains how these methods may help agents retrieve useful experience without loading an unfiltered record of every past interaction.

items.title: Anthropic explores AI-assisted scientific modeling
items.content_text: Anthropic’s Science Blog featured a guest post on AI-assisted scientific modeling, describing how AI can build, fit, and revise models to explore competing explanations of data. The authors emphasize that matching observed data is not by itself scientific understanding; examining alternative models and what the evidence supports matters.

items.title: Claude Code cloud sessions can configure and save repository environments
items.content_text: Anthropic updated Claude Code cloud sessions on Pro, Max, and Ultra to help configure a repository’s environment: Claude determines needed dependencies, network access, and API keys, then saves the setup for future sessions. Anthropic says API keys are saved securely so Claude cannot see them.

items.title: Claude Enterprise adds beta project tags for tracking spend by cost code
items.content_text: Claude Enterprise added beta project tags so eligible organizations can track most project spend against existing codes, such as charge codes or client-matter numbers. This gives organizations another way to attribute and review usage costs without creating a new coding scheme.

items.title: OpenAI closes an initial $11 billion funding tranche at a $1.25 trillion valuation
items.content_text: OpenAI reportedly closed an initial $11 billion tranche of a larger funding round, valuing the company at $1.25 trillion. The round is not described as complete; Reuters reports that the amount raised so far is only part of the company’s original target of up to $30 billion.

items.title: Gemini API routes Embedding 2 Preview requests to the stable model
items.content_text: Effective November 6, requests using `gemini-embedding-2-preview` are routed to `gemini-embedding-2` at the stable model’s rates. Google says the stable model uses the same API schema, pricing, and embedding space, so the transition requires no other code changes or vector re-indexing.

items.title: Google Antigravity adds Gemini Live-powered voice mode
items.content_text: Google introduced voice mode for the Antigravity App and CLI, powered by Gemini Live. Developers can speak tasks, steer work in progress, and answer permission prompts by voice; the post says destructive actions still require on-screen approval.

items.title: Google DeepMind reports AI-agent research on weaknesses in legacy RSA-1024
items.content_text: Google DeepMind reported that human-guided AI agents helped researchers uncover two weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA systems, demonstrating faster ways to stress-test cryptographic assumptions. The researchers said the findings concern obsolete 1024-bit systems; modern protocols that generally use keys of 2048 bits or larger remain secure.

items.title: Meta rolls out Muse Wonder-trained models to Muse and Meta AI
items.content_text: Meta began rolling out specialized versions of its existing models, trained using Muse Wonder, to Muse and Meta AI users. The models bring over Active Memory and Active Focus, which Meta says help them retain relevant context and continue toward goals when unexpected obstacles arise.

items.title: Meta adds customizable Spaces to its Muse AI agent
items.content_text: Meta introduced Spaces, customizable project experiences in its Muse app that can turn a user’s description into a tracker, planner or project board. Users can connect third-party apps so the Spaces update in the background, extending Muse beyond one-off chat interactions.

items.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber for cybersecurity research
items.content_text: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a model it says is more capable at finding and fixing vulnerabilities while better respecting researcher-defined limits. It is initially available through API and Codex to a select group of approved Daybreak Red customers.

items.title: Codex CLI 0.167.0 adds an agent command center and backend switching
items.content_text: Codex CLI 0.167.0 adds an agent command center, including unread-result indicators, and allows users to switch connected backends from the terminal session picker without losing drafts. The release also supports previewing local image attachments while composing.

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab reportedly nears $5 billion funding round
items.content_text: Business Insider reports that Thinking Machines Lab is raising $5 billion at a $40 billion pre-money valuation, with Accel leading the round. The financing was described as nearing completion, but the report does not establish that it has closed or been confirmed by the company.

items.title: Edge 157 upgrades the Copilot new tab page and Copilot experience
items.content_text: Edge 157 adds an upgraded Copilot new tab page that brings search, chat, and web exploration together, with suggested actions and curated work content. Microsoft also updated the Copilot entry points and side pane, including upgraded Copilot Voice and Vision functionality.

items.title: Kling, LTX, and MiniMax video models enter public preview in Microsoft Foundry through fal partnership
items.content_text: Microsoft and fal are bringing Kling v3 Pro, LTX-2.5 Fast, LTX-2.5 Pro, MiniMax H3 Max, and MiniMax H3 Max Turbo to Microsoft Foundry in public preview. The post includes per-second pricing for the models, with rates varying by model, resolution, and (for Kling) audio options.

items.title: Microsoft Foundry extension for Azure Developer CLI reaches GA at version 1.0
items.content_text: Microsoft made the `microsoft.foundry` extension bundle for Azure Developer CLI generally available at version 1.0. It adds agent setup and local testing to the `azd` workflow, with agent and deployment configuration kept alongside application code.

items.title: Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3.1 Pro comes to Microsoft Foundry
items.content_text: Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3.1 Pro, an open-weight model for agentic work with text and image understanding and up to a 1-million-token context window, is coming to Microsoft Foundry. Microsoft lists prices of $2.30 per million input tokens, $0.23 per million cached input tokens, and $11.50 per million output tokens.

items.title: Report: Windows 11 27H2 may be a major OS update as Microsoft sticks with Windows 11
items.content_text: The Verge reports, citing sources, that Microsoft is preparing Windows 11 version 27H2 for 2027 as a full OS swap, with a focus on quality. The report says it remains unclear whether Microsoft will use Windows 12 branding; Microsoft has not confirmed the reported plans.

items.title: Microsoft outlines AI-era Windows vulnerability management and faster remediation
items.content_text: Microsoft describes expanding AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and using AI to help engineers assess impact, identify affected Windows versions, and develop remediation and backport strategies. It also highlights Windows Autopatch through Intune, staged deployments, and hotpatching as ways to reduce the time and disruption involved in deploying protections.

items.title: GitHub Copilot usage metrics API adds code-review details and addressed rate
items.content_text: GitHub added code-review feedback details to enterprise and organization Copilot usage metrics, including counts of comments evaluated and addressed and a per-repository addressed rate. The new breakdowns give administrators more information for assessing Copilot code-review outcomes.

items.title: GitHub Copilot usage metrics API flags telemetry and version gaps
items.content_text: GitHub added per-user telemetry and version-compliance fields, plus aggregate counts, to Copilot usage metrics reports. The additions help administrators identify why usage reports may lack details and which users may need follow-up.

items.title: Microsoft presents Copilot upgrade agent for .NET Windows Arm64 migration
items.content_text: Microsoft described using the GitHub Copilot upgrade agent to assess and update .NET applications for Windows Arm64, including dependencies, platform assumptions, and project configuration. Developers can review proposed changes, but the post notes that a successful build is not a substitute for runtime testing on Windows Arm64.

items.title: GitHub secret scanning adds SpaceX partnership and upgrades detectors
items.content_text: GitHub added SpaceX to its secret-scanning partnership program and introduced detection for a Starlink API secret. It also upgraded detectors for Alibaba, AWS, Google, OpenVSX, Pydantic Services, and Tencent with additional false-positive filtering, expanding coverage and refining alerts.

items.title: Microsoft shows how to run agentic coding locally with Foundry Local and GitHub Copilot
items.content_text: Microsoft described a local agentic-coding workflow that runs Qwen3.8-27B through Foundry Local and connects it to GitHub Copilot. The on-device approach is presented as offering more privacy, predictable inference costs, and continued work without a network connection.

items.title: Anthropic introduces Personal Finance in Claude
items.content_text: Anthropic introduced Personal Finance in Claude, letting users connect selected financial accounts through Plaid and ask questions about balances, transactions, and spending. The feature is read-only, and Anthropic says conversations in its Personal Finance hub are not used to train its models.

items.title: METR estimates AI accelerated Anthropic’s model-capability progress
items.content_text: METR reported that Anthropic’s internal-model benchmark scores had grown at an estimated 1.9 times their prior rate since October 2025, roughly two years of historical progress in one year. METR attributed much of the acceleration to AI-assisted R&D but emphasized substantial uncertainty and possible contributions from other factors.

items.title: Anthropic adds security and admin controls to Claude Enterprise
items.content_text: Anthropic announced Claude Enterprise security and admin updates, including a security center, centralized management, and access controls such as member sign-out through the Admin API and self-managed IP allowlisting. Inference hooks that check prompts and tool calls are generally available, while the security center and centralized management are in beta.

items.title: METR reviews Anthropic’s automated-R&D risk assessment
items.content_text: In a separate review of Anthropic’s August risk report, METR agreed that Anthropic’s internally deployed models posed low direct automated-R&D and acute acceleration risk as of July 15. However, METR said Anthropic’s public report understated the plausibility that acceleration was above its threshold, adding an independent safety-focused assessment alongside METR’s broader acceleration report.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash comes to Google Vids with 15-second generations
items.content_text: Google brought Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash into Google Vids, where users can create clips up to 15 seconds and benefit from improved character consistency and vocal realism. The Workspace post says the rollout began November 5, with availability varying by account and edition.

items.title: Google adds Gemini-powered actionable insights to Forms responses
items.content_text: Google introduced Gemini-powered insights in the Google Forms Responses tab. Gemini analyzes response data to surface trends and recommend next steps, using generated Python code for grounded counts, percentages, and comparisons; the post says the Rapid Release rollout had started November 2, while Scheduled Release rollout is set to start November 19.

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab launches Inkling 2 Small
items.content_text: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Small, a 594B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 17B active parameters, image input and reported gains in agentic coding, vision, knowledge work and reasoning. It is initially available through Tinker with closed weights; the company says it intends to publish Apache 2.0 weights after external safety testing.

items.title: Five9 agrees to acquire Level AI for about $325 million
items.content_text: Five9 agreed to acquire customer-experience AI company Level AI in a cash transaction valued at approximately $325 million. The deal is expected to close in 2026 subject to conditions, and Five9 says Level AI’s applications could be offered to its more than 4,000 customers.

items.title: Box and NVIDIA announce an enterprise AI retrieval engine
items.content_text: Box and NVIDIA announced Box Context Retrieval, a new engine using NVIDIA Nemotron to give AI agents more accurate, permission-aware access to enterprise content across millions of files. Box says it could improve search accuracy and reduce token use and response times; general availability is planned for Enterprise Advanced customers early next year.

items.title: Mistral expands Studio with managed agents, workflows and apps
items.content_text: Mistral expanded Studio with managed agents and apps, plus workflow, enterprise-context, observability and evaluation capabilities. Apps and managed agents are in public preview on Mistral Cloud, while workflows are generally available; Mistral says private-cloud and on-premises deployments will follow at the end of November.

items.title: Anthropic researchers use Claude in mapping a bacteriophage vault structure
items.content_text: Anthropic said its biology team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from a bacteriophage, extending investigation of these little-understood protein structures into viral life. The work is a research result rather than proof of an autonomous AI discovery, and the function of vault particles remains unknown.

items.title: Azure AI Agents azd extension 1.0.0 adds local A2A execution and skill optimization
items.content_text: Version 1.0.0 of Microsoft's Azure AI Agents azd extension adds terminal-only local A2A 0.3 agent execution, including JSON or streaming output. It also adds trace-driven skill optimization and reporting, with generated skills requiring deliberate inspection rather than being automatically applied or deployed.

items.title: Cat Wu joins OpenAI to lead Core Products product management
items.content_text: Cat Wu announced that she is joining OpenAI to lead product management for Core Products, following her departure from Anthropic. This adds a concrete destination and role to the previously reported exit of a Claude Code product leader.

items.title: SpecterOps joins OpenAI Partner Network to bring Daybreak Red to enterprise security teams
items.content_text: SpecterOps announced that it has joined the OpenAI Partner Network and will bring Daybreak Red capabilities to enterprise customers through the Daybreak Defense Network. Its announced services combine OpenAI GPT Cyber Models with security practitioners’ expertise for authorized assessments and security testing.

items.title: OpenAI sets out community commitments and a policy blueprint for AI infrastructure
items.content_text: OpenAI published a National Community Compact for future compute campuses it owns and operates and a policy blueprint proposing greater community input, protection from new costs, and broader sharing of AI infrastructure’s economic benefits. The commitments and proposals address local accountability and the impacts of building and powering data centers.

items.title: Google DeepMind and Singapore’s GovTech launch AntiScam Pango beta
items.content_text: Singapore’s GovTech launched the AntiScam Pango Android beta in collaboration with Google DeepMind, following their work on an on-device scam-detection model. The app flags suspicious messages while keeping private conversations on the user’s device, applying the research in a public-facing tool.

items.title: Preferred Networks releases open-weight PLaMo 3 Translate models
items.content_text: PFN released four open-weight PLaMo 3 Translate models, ranging from 0.8B to 31B parameters, for translation across 53 languages. They can run locally on devices or internal servers, supporting offline translation and keeping source text and output off external cloud servers; use is subject to the PLaMo Community License.

items.title: Mistral AI acquires AI coding-tools startup SkipLabs
items.content_text: Mistral AI acquired SkipLabs, a French startup whose tools aim to make AI code generation faster, more reliable, and more secure; the financial terms were not disclosed. Dealroom reports that SkipLabs' engineers and scientists will join a team led by Mistral co-founder and chief scientist Guillaume Lample, extending Mistral's push beyond model development alone.

items.title: Sand.ai raises $200 million in Series A extension
items.content_text: Video-generation startup Sand.ai raised $200 million in a Series A extension, bringing its 2026 fundraising total to $300 million over 10 months; Dealroom reports the round puts it in unicorn territory. The company plans to use the capital for video-model research, training and inference infrastructure, product development, and overseas expansion.

items.title: Capgemini finds 59% of financial firms pilot or deploy multi-agent AI
items.content_text: Capgemini's World Cloud Report for Financial Services 2027 says 59% of financial institutions surveyed are piloting or deploying multi-agent AI in production, while only 10% have achieved enterprise-wide orchestration. The finding points to rapid experimentation and deployment, but also a substantial gap between pilots and coordinated autonomous operation at scale.

items.title: Chai Discovery and Roche partner on AI-driven drug discovery
items.content_text: Chai Discovery and Roche announced a collaboration to use Chai's AI models and platform in multiple drug-discovery programs across Roche therapeutic areas. The announcement extends the use of AI-based molecular design in pharmaceutical research, although it does not specify financial terms or name the programs.

items.title: Salesforce reports 21-fold Agentforce Coworker usage growth and expands the product
items.content_text: Salesforce announced an expansion of Agentforce Coworker after reporting 21-fold usage growth in three months. New capabilities include connections to Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, broader availability across work environments, and a $50-per-user monthly pricing option.

items.title: Microsoft announces fair-use limits for additional Copilot Chat features
items.content_text: Microsoft is introducing fair-use limits for additional Copilot Chat features for unlicensed users in commercial tenants, across web, desktop, and mobile. The change began November 2 for organizations with 2,000 or fewer Microsoft 365 seats and is scheduled to begin November 9 for larger organizations; Copilot Chat remains included with Microsoft 365 subscriptions, with no admin action required.

items.title: Microsoft details local coding-AI advances for Windows PCs
items.content_text: Microsoft describes how low-bit quantization and systems optimizations make its MAI-Code-1.1-Flash model more practical for local coding workloads on Windows PCs. The post says the 53.0 GiB checkpoint is available through Microsoft Foundry and as a local model in GitHub Copilot on RTX Spark, enabling coding tasks to run on-device rather than relying entirely on per-token cloud usage.

items.title: CodeQL 2.27.4 improves query accuracy, metadata, and CLI security checks
items.content_text: CodeQL 2.27.4 improves query accuracy across several languages, corrects query metadata, and adds security checks when bundling or publishing packs. The CLI also directs JVM warnings and initialization errors to standard error, preventing interference with machine-readable output.

items.title: GitHub Copilot plans to end support for JetBrains IDEs 2025.2.x
items.content_text: Microsoft announced that the GitHub Copilot plugin will end support for JetBrains IDEs version 2025.2.x in the coming months, moving the minimum supported version to 2025.3.x. Existing installations are not expected to be immediately disabled, but users on affected versions may lose compatibility with future plugin updates and will no longer receive new features, fixes, or performance improvements for that IDE version.

items.title: Intelligent Terminal 0.3 adds agent-focused sidebar, session search, and headless mode
items.content_text: Intelligent Terminal 0.3 adds a sidebar for managing tabs and agent sessions, global search, agent filtering, and live status indicators. It can also keep selected tabs running in headless mode after the terminal window closes, and automatically detects supported agent CLIs for the new-tab menu.

items.title: GitHub Copilot becomes available in Xcode’s built-in coding assistant
items.content_text: GitHub Copilot is now available in public preview within Xcode’s built-in coding assistant, starting with Xcode 27.3 beta. The separate GitHub Copilot for Xcode extension remains available, giving developers a native alternative rather than requiring migration.

items.title: Claude Code reduces background subagent status-update usage
items.content_text: Claude Code now uses Haiku 5.5 to write background subagent status updates from short notes instead of rereading the full conversation, which Anthropic says makes each update cost about 99% less. Anthropic estimates sessions with background subagents use about 5% less of the usage limit overall; the change is available to most Pro, Max, and Ultra users and all Team and Enterprise users on v2.1.316 or later.

items.title: Anthropic adds partner agents and products to Claude Marketplace
items.content_text: Anthropic added partner agents and products to Claude Marketplace in security, developer infrastructure, creative work, and productivity. Eligible enterprise customers can apply part of their committed Anthropic spend to the offerings, and the marketplace now has more than 25 partner agents and products.

items.title: Google introduces new Gemini capabilities for its Agentic Data Cloud
items.content_text: Google announced that Gemini can work directly on its borderless Lakehouse, allowing business users to query records across clouds using natural language. The post also describes Gemini agents that can generate and troubleshoot data-engineering workflows and create operational reports, extending Gemini’s enterprise data and analytics capabilities.

items.title: UK says EU AI Act will apply narrowly to AI-integrated goods in Northern Ireland
items.content_text: The UK Government stated that the EU AI Act will apply in Northern Ireland only in a limited, targeted manner, focused on physical products with closely integrated AI systems. The statement distinguishes this scope from wider standalone software and general-purpose AI regulation, which it says are not covered by the Northern Ireland application described.

items.title: Visual Studio Code 1.145 adds remote-agent previews, cron schedules, and chat controls
items.content_text: VS Code 1.145 adds the ability to preview apps and use canvases from remote agent sessions in the Agents window, along with cron-based automation schedules and chat-noise controls. The stable release was dated November 4, 2026.

items.title: Adobe's CX Enterprise Coworker becomes available in Claude
items.content_text: Adobe announced that its CX Enterprise Coworker is now available within Claude, alongside other AI platforms, bringing customer-experience orchestration workflows into tools enterprises already use. Adobe also announced pre-built MCP connectors for integrating with partner systems.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.318 adds mod-consent records and sign-in expiry details
items.content_text: Claude Code v2.1.318 records users’ answers to prompts about enabling session-written mods and exposes stored sign-in expiry in `claude auth status` and `claude -p` JSON results, with warnings before expiry. It also adds `assume_role` support for certain Claude apps gateway AWS upstreams and an effort option for mod model forks.

items.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company to expand Codex’s developer tools
items.content_text: OpenAI announced plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company, whose Code Storage and other developer tools will expand Codex’s code-building, navigation, and review capabilities. The acquisition has not yet closed and remains subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals.

items.title: Daybreak Red with GPT-5.6 Cyber becomes available in AWS GovCloud
items.content_text: OpenAI made GPT-5.6 Cyber available to approved customers in AWS GovCloud (US-East) through Daybreak Red and Amazon Bedrock. The expansion gives eligible government security teams a route to use the model in AWS environments supporting critical missions.

items.title: Tencent releases Hy4 with vision and long-horizon agent capabilities
items.content_text: Tencent released Hy4, adding vision, computer-use, and tool-calling capabilities alongside improvements to long-context understanding and long-horizon agent tasks. Tencent says model weights and system cards will be released in the coming days, so the announcement does not establish that weights are already available.

items.title: Ohio voters pass data-center bans or restrictions in at least 14 municipalities
items.content_text: At least 14 Ohio municipalities voted for data-center bans or other restrictions in November 3 local elections, according to preliminary reporting. The results signal growing local constraints on infrastructure expansion that may affect AI data-center development, though the reported figures are not final certified totals.

items.title: Harvey and Jus Mundi integrate arbitration research agent Jus AI into Harvey
items.content_text: Harvey and Jus Mundi announced a partnership integrating Jus Mundi’s specialized legal-research agent, Jus AI, into Harvey’s Assistant, Agents, Vault, and Workflows. The integration brings arbitration-focused research grounded in Jus Mundi’s database into Harvey’s enterprise legal AI tools.

items.title: CrowdStrike adds detection for abnormal enterprise-agent behavior
items.content_text: CrowdStrike announced Agent Insider Threat Detection to identify abnormal enterprise-agent behavior, including deviations that do not violate an explicit rule, and route them into coordinated investigations. The release also says coordinated multi-agent investigations are now generally available, expanding security monitoring for autonomous agents.

items.title: Microsoft brings GPT-5.6 and expanded Copilot app integration to government clouds
items.content_text: Microsoft announced expanded Copilot capabilities for U.S. Government cloud customers, including GPT-5.6 in GCC, GCC-H, and DoD and editing with Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint across those environments. A simplified, chat-centered Copilot app design is available in GCC and GCC-H, with DoD availability to follow.

items.title: SharePoint tools in Work IQ enter public preview for agents
items.content_text: Microsoft opened a public preview of more than 60 native SharePoint operations through Work IQ, allowing agents to find, understand, create, organize, and share SharePoint content. The tools are also rolling out to Copilot Studio, expanding the SharePoint work agents can perform.

items.title: Microsoft details Windows 11 performance and memory improvements for 8 GB PCs
items.content_text: Microsoft says Windows 11 has memory and performance improvements for 8 GB PCs, reporting up to 20% greater responsiveness and up to 40% faster multitasking in a lab test. The changes include reduced memory use for idle experiences; Microsoft says the latest improvements require Windows 11 version 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later, and notes that actual results and rollout timing may vary.

items.title: WinApp VS Code extension v0.4 previews project-aware WinUI XAML IntelliSense
items.content_text: Microsoft released WinApp VS Code extension v0.4, adding an experimental preview of project-aware IntelliSense for WinUI XAML, a command to create WinUI apps, and the ability to build and run projects from VS Code. The extension is available in public preview, with full project-aware support for C# WinUI projects requiring the .NET 10 SDK.

items.title: Dependabot version updates add support for Agent Package Manager
items.content_text: Dependabot now supports version updates for Agent Package Manager dependencies, opening pull requests for supported Git dependencies declared in apm.yml and regenerating apm.lock.yaml when present. The feature is generally available on github.com across plans; this update does not include security updates.

items.title: Copilot usage API separates BYOK and enterprise custom-model usage
items.content_text: GitHub updated the Copilot usage metrics API to separately identify local BYOK activity and requests using enterprise custom models. The added reporting helps organizations review model usage and distinguish provider-billed or local-model use from Copilot-hosted usage; existing totals remain unchanged.

items.title: Dependabot adds support for Python 3.15
items.content_text: Dependabot now supports Python 3.15, allowing projects using the new version to continue receiving updates. GitHub says support is available to all github.com users and will be included in GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24.

items.title: Claude Code product lead Cat Wu announces her departure from Anthropic
items.content_text: Cat Wu announced that the previous Friday was her last day at Anthropic, where she led product for Claude Code. She thanked the teams and users and reflected on the product's growth; her post did not give a reason for leaving.

items.title: Claude adds auto-connect for plugins using Claude as a trusted issuer
items.content_text: Anthropic announced a beta that lets compatible MCP-server plugins auto-connect when users log in to Claude, reducing repeated sign-in and authorization steps. ClaudeDevs says the feature is in beta for Team and Enterprise plans.

items.title: Anthropic adds text watermarking for Claude Mythos 5, Opus 4.7, and Sonnet 4.6
items.content_text: Anthropic's November 3 platform notes say text generated by Claude Mythos 5, Opus 4.7, and Sonnet 4.6 carries its text watermark on supported platforms. The notes caution that Sonnet 4.6 outputs may not carry the watermark when temperature, top_p, or top_k is set to a non-default value.

items.title: OpenAI appoints Jill Hazelbaker as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer
items.content_text: OpenAI appointed Jill Hazelbaker as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer, where she will lead global communications and corporate positioning. She will work with company leaders on public understanding of AI and trust in OpenAI’s mission.
